questions.statement: A sovereign wealth fund has a strict regulatory requirement mandating that cryptographic encryption keys must be generated, stored, and managed inside dedicated, single-tenant FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) directly under the sole physical and logical control of the company's security officers. AWS personnel must have zero administrative access to the HSM key material. Which AWS service meets these compliance requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to provision and automatically renew public SSL/TLS certificates.
options.explanation: Incorrect: ACM manages SSL/TLS public certificates, not custom corporate symmetric HSM encryption keys.

options.text: Deploy an AWS CloudHSM cluster inside a private VPC to manage single-tenant FIPS 140-2 Level 3 cryptographic hardware.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS CloudHSM provides dedicated, single-tenant FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated hardware security modules running in your VPC where the customer has sole ownership and control of cryptographic keys and HSM user administration.

options.text: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) with multi-tenant default key stores
options.explanation: Incorrect: Standard AWS KMS uses multi-tenant HSMs validated to FIPS 140-2 Level 3 (or Level 2) managed by AWS, rather than dedicated customer-administered single-tenant appliances.

options.text: Store application configuration feature flags in AWS Secrets Manager and schedule automatic secret rotation.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Secrets Manager stores database credentials and API keys, relying on KMS or CloudHSM for key encryption.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS CloudHSM provides fully managed, dedicated single-tenant hardware security modules (HSMs) under customer control for strict regulatory and FIPS 140-2 Level 3 compliance.

options.text: Configure AWS Billing Conductor to define custom billing groups, apply pricing markups, and generate pro forma invoices.

options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS Budgets sends spending alerts, but does not calculate custom rate markups or generate pro forma billing invoices.

questions.statement: An enterprise needs to implement centralized outbound internet egress inspection for 80 VPCs across 2 AWS Regions. All outbound web requests must be inspected against TLS Server Name Indication (SNI) domain whitelists and intrusion prevention system (IPS) Suricata rule sets. The solution must scale to 45 Gbps of egress traffic per region with high availability across 3 Availability Zones and zero single point of failure. Which architecture should be deployed?

options.text: Deploy a centralized Egress Inspection VPC in each region containing an AWS Transit Gateway attachment with Appliance Mode enabled, and deploy AWS Network Firewall endpoints in a dedicated firewall subnet in each Availability Zone backed by a stateful rule group for domain list SNI filtering and IPS Suricata rules.
options.explanation: Correct: Centralized egress inspection via AWS Transit Gateway with Appliance Mode and AWS Network Firewall endpoints across 3 AZs scales up to 100 Gbps, provides stateful SNI domain filtering, and eliminates single points of failure.

options.text: Deploy squid proxy EC2 instances on a single t3.medium instance in each spoke VPC.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Self-managed proxy instances on t3.medium cannot handle 45 Gbps, create single points of failure, and introduce massive operational maintenance.

options.text: Configure Amazon Route 53 private hosted zones in each VPC with wildcard records pointing to 127.0.0.1.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Route 53 DNS sinkholing does not provide stateful Layer 7 IPS packet inspection or SNI filtering for active TCP flows.

options.text: Create VPC Peering connections between all 80 VPCs and deploy NAT Gateways in every spoke subnet.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Deploying NAT Gateways in hundreds of spoke subnets is extremely expensive and lacks centralized stateful IPS/SNI inspection.

questions.generalExplanation: Centralized egress VPC architecture with AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Network Firewall provides scalable, highly available Layer 7 domain filtering and Suricata-compatible IPS inspection.

pt.statement: Uma empresa precisa implementar a inspeção centralizada de saída de tráfego de internet (egress) para 80 VPCs em 2 regiões da AWS. Todas as solicitações web de saída devem ser inspecionadas em relação a listas de permissão de domínios TLS Server Name Indication (SNI) e conjuntos de regras Suricata de sistema de prevenção contra intrusões (IPS). A solução deve ter capacidade de escalar até 45 Gbps de tráfego de saída por região com alta disponibilidade em 3 Zonas de Disponibilidade e nenhum ponto único de falha. Qual arquitetura deve ser implantada?

options.text: Implantar uma VPC de inspeção de saída centralizada em cada região contendo um anexo do AWS Transit Gateway com o Appliance Mode ativado e implantar endpoints do AWS Network Firewall em uma sub-rede de firewall dedicada em cada Zona de Disponibilidade, com suporte de um grupo de regras com estado (stateful) para filtragem SNI de domínios e regras Suricata de IPS.
options.explanation: Correto: A inspeção centralizada de saída via AWS Transit Gateway com Appliance Mode e endpoints do AWS Network Firewall em 3 AZs escala até 100 Gbps, fornece filtragem stateful de domínios SNI e elimina pontos únicos de falha.

options.text: Implantar instâncias EC2 com proxy squid em uma única instância t3.medium em cada VPC spoke.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Instâncias de proxy autogerenciadas em t3.medium não suportam 45 Gbps, criam pontos únicos de falha e introduzem enorme sobrecarga operacional de manutenção.

options.text: Configurar zonas hospedadas privadas do Amazon Route 53 em cada VPC com registros curinga apontando para 127.0.0.1.
options.explanation: Incorreto: O sinkholing de DNS via Route 53 não fornece inspeção stateful de pacotes na Camada 7 (IPS) nem filtragem SNI para fluxos TCP ativos.

options.text: Criar conexões de VPC Peering entre todas as 80 VPCs e implantar NAT Gateways em cada sub-rede spoke.
options.explanation: Incorreto: Implantar NAT Gateways em centenas de sub-redes spoke é extremamente caro e não oferece inspeção centralizada de IPS/SNI com estado.

pt.generalExplanation: A arquitetura de VPC de saída centralizada com AWS Transit Gateway e AWS Network Firewall oferece filtragem de domínios na Camada 7 escalável e altamente disponível, além de inspeção IPS compatível com Suricata.

questions.domainName: Domain 1: Design Solutions for Organizational Complexity
questions.statement: An automated data processing pipeline running on an EC2 instance in Account A needs to access an Amazon S3 bucket in Account B. For enhanced security, Account B requires that the IAM role in Account A must provide an External ID when assuming the cross-account role to prevent the 'Confused Deputy' problem. How should the IAM trust policy in Account B be configured?

options.text: Create an IAM user in Account B with an access key and send the plaintext secret key to Account A via email.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Distributing static long-term IAM credentials violates security best practices and does not solve the confused deputy vulnerability.

options.text: Add a public read/write bucket policy on the S3 bucket in Account B.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Making the bucket public exposes all data to the internet.

options.text: Configure the trust policy of the IAM role in Account B with an `sts:AssumeRole` action, specifying Account A's role as the Principal, and add a `Condition` block requiring `sts:ExternalId` matching the shared unique identifier string.
options.explanation: Correct: The Confused Deputy problem is mitigated by requiring the third-party/cross-account role assumption to supply an `sts:ExternalId` in the `Condition` block of the IAM role's trust policy.

options.text: Configure VPC Peering and disable IAM authorization entirely.
options.explanation: Incorrect: VPC Peering operates at the network layer and does not bypass or configure IAM role trust authorization.

questions.generalExplanation: Using an External ID in the `Condition` block of an IAM role's trust policy is the standard AWS mechanism to prevent the Confused Deputy problem during cross-account role assumption.

options.text: Point all 1,000 EC2 instances across all accounts directly to on-premises domain controller IP addresses over the public internet.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Exposing Active Directory ports over the public internet is a major security vulnerability and creates high network latency.

options.text: Create local Windows Administrator users on every EC2 instance using EC2 User Data.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Local user management on 1,000 instances lacks centralized domain governance, GPOs, and Kerberos SSO.

options.text: Deploy Amazon Cognito User Pools and configure Windows login via OAuth 2.0.

questions.generalExplanation: AWS Managed Microsoft AD shared across accounts combined with a forest trust and AWS Systems Manager Seamless Domain Join provides a scalable, highly available enterprise directory architecture.

questions.statement: A multinational financial enterprise stores 10 petabytes of historical transaction files in an Amazon S3 bucket in us-east-1. options.text: Enable S3 Versioning on both buckets, configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) with KMS encryption options and a destination KMS key specified, and initiate an Amazon S3 Batch Replication job to replicate the pre-existing objects.
options.explanation: Correct: Standard S3 CRR replicates only newly uploaded objects after the rule is created. Replicating existing objects requires creating an Amazon S3 Batch Replication job in addition to configuring CRR with SSE-KMS permissions.

options.text: Enable S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) and wait 24 hours for AWS to automatically synchronize all historical objects.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Standard S3 CRR rules do NOT automatically replicate objects that existed prior to rule creation without an S3 Batch Replication job.

options.text: Use the AWS CLI command `aws s3 cp` on an EC2 t3.nano instance over the public internet.
options.explanation: Incorrect: An EC2 t3.nano instance will run out of memory, take months to transfer 10 PB over the internet, and cost substantially more than native S3 Batch Replication.

options.text: Change the storage class of the source bucket to S3 Glacier Flexible Archive to trigger automatic cross-region mirroring.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Storage class transitions do not replicate data across AWS regions.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon S3 Batch Replication allows you to replicate existing objects that were stored in a bucket prior to configuring S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR).

questions.statement: A financial banking institution must store regulatory SEC Rule 17a-4 transaction records in Amazon S3 for a mandatory retention period of 5 years. options.text: Apply an S3 Bucket Policy with an explicit Deny for `s3:DeleteObject` covering all IAM users.
options.explanation: Incorrect: The AWS account root user or an administrator with IAM privileges can modify or delete the bucket policy to bypass the restriction.

options.text: Configure an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 Lifecycle transitions change storage class, but do not prevent deletion by authorized users unless Object Lock is enabled.

options.text: Enable Amazon S3 Object Lock in Governance Mode with a 5-year retention period.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Governance Mode allows users with specific IAM permissions (s3:BypassGovernanceRetention) or root to alter or delete protected objects.

options.text: Enable S3 Versioning on the bucket and configure Amazon S3 Object Lock in Compliance Mode with a default retention period of 5 years.
options.explanation: Correct: S3 Object Lock in Compliance Mode enforces a strict WORM (Write Once, Read Many) model where no user, including the root user in the AWS account, can delete objects or reduce retention during the compliance period.

options.text: Use AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway to mirror the database.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Storage Gateway does not convert schemas between heterogeneous database engines (SQL Server to PostgreSQL).
